fish.table_1a_title: Microbiological Requirements for Fish and Fishery products - Hygiene Indicator Organisms
fish.table_1b_title: Microbiological Requirements for Fish and Fishery products - Safety Indicator Organisms

categories.name: Chilled/Frozen Finfish
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature Control along value chain
categories.definition: Clean and wholesome finfish in raw, chilled or frozen condition; freezing must bring the thermal centre to -18°C or lower after thermal stabilisation.

categories.name: Chilled/Frozen Crustaceans
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature Control along value chain
categories.definition: Clean whole or peeled crustaceans (shrimp/prawn, crabs and lobster) in raw, chilled or frozen condition.

categories.name: Chilled/Frozen Cephalopods
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature Control along value chain
categories.definition: Cleaned whole or de-skinned cephalopods (squid, cuttlefish and octopus) in raw, chilled or frozen condition.

categories.name: Live Bivalve Molluscs
notes: No hygienic indicators are currently prescribed for Live Bivalve Molluscs.
categories.definition: Oyster, clam, mussel, scallop or abalone alive immediately prior to consumption, with controls over approved/classified harvest areas and purification where applicable.

categories.name: Chilled/Frozen Bivalves
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature Control along value chain
categories.definition: Clean whole or shucked bivalves in chilled or frozen condition, including oysters, mussels, clams, cockles and scallops.

categories.name: Frozen Cooked Crustaceans/Frozen Heat Shucked Mollusc
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Selection of raw material; Time-Temperature Control along value chain; process control
categories.definition: Frozen cooked crustaceans or frozen heat-shucked mollusca; cooked crustaceans use a defined time/temperature process, while heat-shucked bivalves are mildly heated before shucking and subsequently frozen.

categories.name: Dried/Salted and Dried Fishery Products
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Selection of raw material; Adequate drying (water activity <= 0.78)
categories.definition: Fishery products prepared from fresh/wholesome finfish or shellfish after drying with or without salt.

categories.name: Thermally Processed Fishery Products

clostridium_botulinum.requirement: Absence of viable spores or vegetative cells of Clostridium botulinum and absence of botulinum toxin.

notes: Commercial sterility should be established as per APHA (2015), Canned Foods - Tests for Commercial Sterility, Compendium of Methods for the Microbiological Examination of Food.
categories.definition: Fishery products heat processed for sufficient time to achieve commercial sterility in hermetically sealed containers.

categories.name: Fermented Fishery Products
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Selection of raw material

clostridium_botulinum.requirement: Absence of viable spores or vegetative cells of Clostridium botulinum and absence of botulinum toxin.

categories.definition: Fish products undergoing degradative changes through enzymatic or microbiological activity, with or without salt; includes accelerated fermentation, acid ensilage and chemical hydrolysis products.

categories.name: Smoked Fishery Products
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature Control along value chain
categories.definition: Fish/fishery products treated with smoke; the category refers to hot-smoked fish with complete coagulation of flesh proteins.

categories.name: Accelerated Freeze Dried Fishery Products
categories.action: Selection of raw material; Improvement in hygiene; along value chain
categories.definition: Fish, shrimp or fishery products rapidly frozen and dried under high vacuum by sublimation to final moisture below two percent.

categories.name: Fish Mince/Surimi and Analogues
categories.action: Selection of raw material; Improvement in hygiene
categories.definition: Comminuted mechanically removed fish meat essentially free from bones, viscera and skin; includes surimi and surimi analogues.

categories.name: Fish Pickle
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Control of pH/acidity; selection of ingredients
categories.definition: Oily semi-solid fish pickle with spices and acidic taste, prepared by frying edible fish portions and maturation with vinegar/organic acids.

categories.name: Battered and Breaded Fishery Products

listeria_monocytogenes.notes: Stored exactly as printed in Appendix B Version 2.

categories.definition: Fish portions, fillets or mince coated with batter and/or breading.

categories.name: Convenience Fishery Products
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Time-Temperature control of batter mix
categories.definition: Ready-to-eat tertiary fish products and fish snacks for direct human consumption with minimal handling; includes sous-vide cooked products, cooked in-pack surimi products, pasteurised crab meat and pasteurised molluscs.

categories.name: Powdered Fish Based Products
categories.action: Improvement in hygiene; Selection of raw material
categories.definition: Powdered products prepared from finfish/shellfish or parts thereof, with or without other edible ingredients, for direct use, supplementation or rehydration.

hygiene.coagulase_positive_staphylococci: IS 5887 Part 2 or IS 5887 Part 8 (Sec 1) / ISO 6888-1 or IS 5887 Part 8 (Sec 2) / ISO 6888-2

safety.vibrio_cholerae_o1_o139: Vibrio, Bacteriological Analytical Manual, Chapter 9, USFDA BAM Online, May 2004

source_notes: Commercial sterility should be established as per APHA (2015), Canned Foods - Tests for Commercial Sterility, Compendium of Methods for the Microbiological Examination of Food.
No hygienic indicators are currently prescribed for Live Bivalve Molluscs.
For Battered and Breaded Fishery Products, the Listeria monocytogenes sampling plan is stored as n=5, c=5, Absent/25g exactly as printed in Version 2; PMSV does not silently alter it.

stage_rules.process_hygiene: Applicable at the end of the manufacturing process; process-hygiene criteria indicate acceptable functioning of the production process and are not market-release criteria.
stage_rules.food_safety: Food-safety criteria define acceptability of a batch/lot and apply at the end of manufacturing and to products in the market during shelf-life.

action_on_unsatisfactory_process_hygiene: Check and improve process hygiene by implementation of Schedule 4 (Part III) hygiene guidelines.
Ensure that all applicable food-safety criteria in Table 2B are complied with.
milk.proprietary_dairy_rule: Microbiological standards also apply to proprietary dairy foods depending on their analogy as determined by FSSAI with the product categories in Tables 2A and 2B.

sampling_plan_definitions.n: Number of units comprising a sample.
sampling_plan_definitions.c: Maximum allowable number of units having microbiological counts above m for a 2-class plan and between m and M for a 3-class plan.
sampling_plan_definitions.m: Microbiological limit separating unsatisfactory from satisfactory in a 2-class plan or acceptable from satisfactory in a 3-class plan.
sampling_plan_definitions.M: Microbiological limit separating unsatisfactory from satisfactory in a 3-class plan.

two_class: Satisfactory if all values observed are <= m.
Unsatisfactory if one or more values are > m or more than c values are > m.
three_class: Satisfactory if all values observed are <= m.
Acceptable if a maximum of c values are between m and M and the rest are <= m.
Unsatisfactory if one or more values are > M or more than c values are > m.

reference_methods.staphylococcus_aureus: IS 5887 Part 2; or IS 5887 Part 8 (Sec 1) / ISO 6888-1; or IS 5887 Part 8 (Sec 2) / ISO 6888-2
reference_methods.listeria_monocytogenes: ISO 11290-1/-2 and IS 14988 Part 1/Part 2, as applicable

source_notes: Latest version of the reference test method shall apply. Where an ISO method adopted by BIS is specified, the latest ISO method or BIS equivalent, if available, shall apply.
FSSAI Manual of Methods of Analysis of Foods (Microbiological Testing) may also be referred to along with the specified IS/ISO methods.
Regulatory sampling follows the Appendix B sampling instructions, including the no-retesting/no-resampling provision stated in Version 2.

meat.table_5a_title: Microbiological Standards for Meat and Meat Products - Process Hygiene Criteria
meat.table_5b_title: Microbiological Standards for Meat & Meat Products - Food Safety Criteria

categories.name: Fresh meat / Chilled meat
categories.definition: Fresh meat has not been treated to ensure preservation. Chilled meat is fresh meat washed with potable water and kept between 0–7°C.
notes: Products in categories 1–5 are to be cooked to make safe before consumption.

categories.name: Frozen meat
categories.definition: Fresh meat washed with potable water, chilled and frozen so the product reaches -18°C or colder at the thermal centre after thermal stabilization.
notes: Products in categories 1–5 are to be cooked to make safe before consumption.

categories.name: Raw marinated/minced/comminuted meat
categories.definition: Meat with or without bones reduced to fragments by cutting, grinding, dicing, chopping or milling and/or marinated, with or without additives.
notes: The Yeast and Mold Count values 1×10^4 and 5×10^4 cfu/g are stored from the amended values printed in Appendix B Version 2.
Products in categories 1–5 are to be cooked to make safe before consumption.

categories.name: Semi-cooked / Smoked Meat / meat food Product
categories.definition: Partially heat-treated and/or smoked meat or meat product requiring additional heat treatment before consumption.
notes: Products in categories 1–5 are to be cooked to make safe before consumption.

categories.name: Cured/Pickled meat
categories.definition: Meat product prepared after curing/pickling in solution containing salt, nitrate/nitrite and adjuncts for preservation and desired colour, flavour and shelf life.
notes: Products in categories 1–5 are to be cooked to make safe before consumption.

categories.name: Fermented meat products
categories.definition: Chopped or ground meat products aged through desirable microorganisms to develop low pH and characteristic flavour, taste, texture and long shelf life.

categories.name: Dried/dehydrated meat products
categories.definition: Meat or meat products in which part of the free water has been removed by evaporation or sublimation.

categories.name: Cooked Meat Products
categories.definition: Meat or meat product subjected to heat treatment achieving a minimum thermal core temperature of 75°C.

categories.name: Canned/Retort pouch Meat Products
categories.definition: Meat product packed in hermetically sealed containers and heat treated after sealing sufficiently to make the product shelf stable.

conditional.reason: The FSSAI product standard includes raw, partially cooked and fully cooked frozen shrimp. Appendix B separates chilled/frozen crustaceans from frozen cooked crustaceans.
The FSSAI product standard allows raw or cooked frozen lobster. Appendix B separates chilled/frozen crustaceans from frozen cooked crustaceans.
The FSSAI product standard contains raw frozen and cooked frozen clam-meat variants. Appendix B separates chilled/frozen bivalves from frozen heat-shucked/cooked molluscs.
